title: Bridge Captain Book Series

contributors.contribution: Worked from my universe, lore, story framework, characters, factions, technology, and broad narrative direction to turn the Bridge Captain setting into novel-length prose.

description: I expanded the Bridge Captain game universe into a six-book science-fiction series by creating the underlying setting, lore, factions, technology, characters, conflicts, and broad story framework. I then collaborated with a California science-fiction writer through Heavy Cat Media to turn that material into novel-length prose. All six books were released on Amazon under the Michael Carter pen name, with Square Particle publishing the series.

sections.title: From Game Backstory to Science-Fiction Universe
paragraphs: The book series grew out of my work on Bridge Captain and my desire to give the game a much deeper history and fictional universe.

Rather than treating the game's story as a small amount of background text, I developed a broader setting with its own history, factions, political relationships, technology, ships, characters, conflicts, and military structure.

sections.title: Universe & Story Development
paragraphs: I created the underlying universe, lore, major story direction, and broad narrative framework before working with an outside writer on the prose.
My contribution centered on what the universe was, how it worked, the conflicts taking place within it, and the science-fiction and military concepts that supported the larger Bridge Captain setting.

sections.title: Six-Book Series
paragraphs: The collaboration ultimately produced six complete science-fiction books.
All six books were released through Amazon, turning the Bridge Captain setting into a published cross-media property rather than leaving the worldbuilding solely inside the game.

sections.title: Technical Space Combat
paragraphs: A major part of the setting was ship-based tactical warfare.

The books developed battles around command decisions, sensors, weapons, missiles, propulsion, reactors, fleet positioning, damage, boarding, jump-gate travel, and the operational behavior of ships and crews.

sections.title: Factions, Fleets & Political Structure
paragraphs: The series expanded Bridge Captain beyond a single ship or crew by establishing competing governments, military forces, fleets, alliances, enemies, and historical conflicts.
This gave the game universe a larger strategic context in which individual ships and captains could operate.

sections.title: Cross-Media Worldbuilding
paragraphs: The books and game were conceived as parts of the same broader science-fiction IP.
The book project let me explore history, politics, characters, technology, and large-scale conflicts that would have been difficult to communicate entirely through the game itself.

sections.title: Working with an Outside Writer
paragraphs: I collaborated with a California science-fiction writer associated with Heavy Cat Media to convert my story framework and worldbuilding into full novel prose.
That required communicating the underlying rules of the setting, major plot direction, characters, technology, and intended tone while another creator handled the detailed prose writing.

sections.title: Michael Carter Pen Name
paragraphs: The books were released under the Michael Carter pen name rather than my personal name.
The pen name was used on the recommendation of the California media company involved in the project.

sections.title: Square Particle Publishing
paragraphs: Square Particle published the completed books and released them through Amazon.
The surviving ebook metadata identifies Square Particle as the publisher, connecting the series directly to the same independent studio behind Bridge Captain.

sections.title: Bridge Captain IP Development
paragraphs: The book series became another branch of Bridge Captain's development rather than a separate unrelated writing project.
It reflects my interest in designing not only games and game systems, but the larger fictional worlds, technology, history, and conflicts that give those systems context.

historicalNotes: The book series was created to expand the Bridge Captain backstory and fictional universe.
Jamie created the underlying universe, lore, story outline, broad narrative direction, factions, technology, conflicts, and worldbuilding.
A California science-fiction writer handled the detailed prose.
The writer was associated with Heavy Cat Media and was its CEO.
Jamie also remembers Palace in the Sky Productions LLC being associated with the writer/company relationship.
The exact business relationship between Heavy Cat Media and Palace in the Sky Productions LLC should not be stated more specifically without additional documentation.
Jamie attempted to participate in editing the manuscripts but did not have final editorial control over the prose.
Do not publicly frame disagreements over editing or prose quality negatively; they are private historical context only.
The Michael Carter author name was a pen name rather than Jamie's personal name.
Jamie remembers being advised by the California media company not to publish the books under his real name.
Recovered MOBI files form a six-book sequence and contain complete chapter structures.
Recovered ebook metadata identifies Michael Carter as author and Square Particle as publisher.
All six books have now been confirmed by Jamie as currently listed on Amazon.
The series contains substantial recurring science-fiction worldbuilding involving starships, crews, factions, political structures, military organizations, technologies, and continuing conflicts.
Technical and tactical starship combat is a significant recurring component of the books.
Recurring operational concepts include sensors, fleet actions, missiles, reactors, jump-gate travel, tactical positioning, ship damage, boarding, command decisions, and crew operations.
The books should be treated as an extension of the Bridge Captain IP rather than as an unrelated publishing project.
Public attribution must distinguish Jamie's universe/story/worldbuilding work from the contracted writer's prose authorship.
